tob-13509: This volume of the fourteen-volume Sacred Books of the East series gathers the literature of medieval Arabic, Moorish, and Turkish civilization. Readers meet the poets of Baghdad and Córdoba, the philosophers of the Islamic golden age, and the storytellers of the Ottoman court. It opens a window onto a millennium of Islamic letters.
tob-0009: This old text, fathered on the Bible’s Enoch, tells of angels who fell to earth and the sights shown to the upright seer. Though kept out of the Bible, it deeply shaped Jewish and Christian pictures of heaven, hell, and the last day. R. H. Charles’s Englishing is the classic version.
tob-4009: Tommaso Campanella dreamed this ideal city from a jail cell — a realm ruled by priest-sages, where goods are shared and the stars order all counsels. Set down in 1602 as he awaited death, it pictures a perfected Catholic commonwealth. The book stands with More’s Utopia among the great dream-states.
tob-0109: Basil Valentine’s Last Will binds his parting gold-lore — workmanlike receipts, the bequest of his craft, and warnings to unmeet seekers. The work rounds his printed writings. It shows the cloister-monk’s hand at its plainest. Seekers prized it as his farewell gift to the art.
tob-4109: T. W. Rhys Davids’s Milinda gives the famed talk between the Greek king Menander and the Buddhist sage Nagasena. Their moot on the self and rebirth is a crown-piece of Buddhist thought. The volume is a jewel of the Sacred Books of the East.
tob-4309: Robert Ernest Hume’s Thirteen Chief Upanishads — 1921 — is the standard one-book English Upanishads, Englished from Sanskrit with scholar’s care. His clear hand made the forest word on the Self open to all. The volume stays the classic English gathering.
tob-9409: More’s Englishing of Ovid’s Shape-Book gives the great Roman song of changings — gods, wood-maids, and heroes turned to beast, bird, and tree. The poem molded western art and letters. This printing bears Ovid’s wit and ruth to English readers.
tob-12909: Swami Vivekananda’s Raja Yoga — 1896 — introduced Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras to the Western world. His commentary and lectures on breath control made the royal path practical. The book launched yoga in America. It remains the classic introduction to meditation’s royal road.
arxiv-2605-08809: Pretraining a language model is mostly about predicting the next word, but the shape of its internal word-embeddings matters too. Yan Sun and colleagues propose SimReg, an embedding-similarity regularization added to pretraining so that related tokens sit closer together in the model's inner space. The 2026 paper argues this simple addition lifts performance on downstream tasks.
arxiv-2605-09009: Chatbots can decide step by step, but in-context learning alone makes them shaky decision-makers. Minmin Zhang, Sina Aghaei, and Soroush Saghafian improve sequential decision-making by adding supervised fine-tuning to the in-context mix. The 2026 paper teaches language models to decide, not just chat.
arxiv-2605-09109: Reinforcement learners can phone an expert for advice, but experts err too. Yann Berthelot, Philippe Preux, and Riad Akrour diagnose query-time expert-guided reinforcement learning: when to trust the expert, and how. The 2026 paper is about using advice wisely in machine learning.
arxiv-2605-09209: Bilevel optimization nests problems, and when the inner problem has many solutions — a manifold of them — differentiation gets hairy. Saeed Masiha, Zebang Shen, Negar Kiyavash, and Niao He select first, then differentiate. The 2026 paper is optimization for nested problems with non-unique inner answers.
arxiv-2605-09509: Reconstructing a full matrix from single-bit observations — yes or no, like or dislike — is matrix completion at its stingiest. Takeru Matsuda brings empirical Bayes machinery to the 1-bit case. The 2026 paper is statistics for recommendation systems running on minimal data.
arxiv-2605-09609: Polynomial neural networks were thought to have minimal architectures filling a given function space. Kevin Dao and Jose Israel Rodriguez find counterexamples, search the frontier, and catalog the defects. The 2026 paper is algebraic deep learning on what minimal really means.
arxiv-2605-09709: Superintegrable systems — blessed with more conserved quantities than degrees of freedom — can make exquisitely sensitive rotation sensors. Leandro Hayato Ymai, Karin Wittmann Wilsmann, and colleagues propose exactly such a sensor. The 2026 paper is exquisite quantum sensing born from mathematical physics.
arxiv-2605-09909: Variational quantum eigensolvers get stuck in barren plateaus — flat, uninformative optimization landscapes where gradients vanish; symmetry-protected basin localization keeps them in fertile ground. Yangshuai Wang develops the technique. The 2026 paper is quantum computing optimization that respects symmetry. It keeps variational optimizers in the fertile valleys.
arxiv-2605-10009: Style-adaptive retrieval via dynamic SVD modulation, driven by hypernetworks — Hystar. Yujia Cai, Boxuan Li, Chenghao Xu, and Jiexi Yan build the retrieval system. The 2026 paper is retrieval that adapts its style. It retrieves with dynamically adaptive, hypernetwork-driven style.
arxiv-2605-10409: Photorealistic simplification, done progressively — detail that melts away gracefully. Adi Rosenthal, Dana Berman, Yedid Hoshen, and Ariel Shamir develop the method. The 2026 paper is computer graphics. It simplifies complex 3D scenes progressively while always remaining completely photorealistic. The graphics stay beautiful.
pmc-13453809: Dynamic platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio trajectories — grouped by trajectory modeling — associated with short-term outcomes and survival. pmc-13421209: Acute complexity in older patients — recognized by Reach, a predictive machine learning model for patient prioritisation. pmc-13516009: Thailand's border provinces — wildlife consumption, contact, and environmental exposures across ethnic communities, in a quantitative One Health study. pmc-13421809: Endochondral ossification — its proteomic dynamics, with insights from antler tip analysis. Xi Xi, Xinyue Cao, Yuying Zhou, and colleagues profile the antlers. arxiv-2606-17009: Jing-Rui Shi, Jiang-Tao Zhang, and Ye Xing study exotic particles made of two mesons stuck together. arxiv-2606-17609: Rui Wen and colleagues expose the benchmark illusion: pruned LLMs can pass multiple choice but fail to answer. Compression that preserves test scores may destroy real capability. arxiv-2606-17709: C. Benito and colleagues optimize bias-tailored quantum error correction beyond code-capacity noise. Real qubits have biased errors, and codes tuned to the bias perform better. arxiv-2606-17809: András Biricz and colleagues analyze pollen at million scale with multimodal microscopy and expert-guided foundation models. arxiv-2606-18209: Trisha Mittal, Akshay Mehra, and Joshua Kimball rethink dataset distillation for classification, asking whether distilled sets outperform coresets. plos-pone-0003409: Ovarian cancer researchers found the immune system recognizing tumors in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003509: Immunologists decoded a two-key system for antibody class-switching in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003609: Parasitologists found a quality-control protein moonlighting in Giardia in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003709: In 2008, Seko, Azuma, and Takahashi found the eye's white keeping old company. The human sclera, the tough coat guarding the eyeball, shares deep traits with cartilage across evolution. The kinship reframes the sclera as a cartilage cousin, with hints for treating its diseases.
plos-pone-0003809: Paulson, Galipeau, and Xu charted mutations in a precancerous esophagus in this 2008 paper. The p16 tumor suppressor gene showed a characteristic mutation spectrum in Barrett's esophagus. The pattern marks the genetic road from chronic reflux to cancer.
plos-pone-0003909: In 2008, Horita, Frankel, and Thorburn built a targeted toxin for acute myeloid leukemia. The fusion toxin homed in on AML cells and killed them through two death programs at once. plos-pone-0004009: In 2008, Ren, Pan, and Parvez repurposed a leprosy drug against immune overdrive. Clofazimine blocked the Kv1.3 potassium channel by disturbing calcium oscillations in T cells. plos-pone-0004109: In 2008, Foygel, Choi, and Jun gave Oct4 a new starring role in embryos. The famous stem-cell factor also steered the maternal-to-embryonic transition. Early embryos reprogrammed their gene network under Oct4's command. The finding extends Oct4's reach to life's first hours.
plos-pone-0004209: In 2009, Mandairon, Poncelet, and Bensafi found human and mouse noses agreeing. Humans and mice showed strikingly similar smell preferences overall. Pleasant and nasty smells ranked alike in both species tested. The shared hedonic scale hints at common smell wiring underneath.
plos-pone-0004309: In 2009, Slominski, Zmijewski, and Semak traced a vitamin D cousin's fate. Adrenal glands converted 7-dehydrocholesterol through steroidal 5,7-dienes. The sequential metabolism ran fast outside the body. The pathway widens vitamin D biology. The finding may reshape views of adrenal steroid making.
plos-pone-0004409: In 2009, Belin, Kaya, and Duisit found vitamin C starving tumors. Ascorbic acid slowed tumor growth by shutting down cell-cycle genes. The vitamin silenced key growth genes. The finding reframes vitamin C in cancer research. The high dose made the difference.
plos-pone-0004509: In 2009, a team brewed tricky cell antennas in vats. Big batches of lab-made human scent receptors were cleaned up. The tough antenna proteins were coaxed soluble. The method now serves drug hunt pipelines. The receptors sit in greasy cell walls.
plos-pone-0004609: In 2009, Capellini, McNamara, and Preston asked whether sleep cements memories. Sleep's role in memory consolidation was tested across mammals. plos-pone-0004709: In 2009, Stauch, Dernier, and Sarmiento Marchese found transplant drugs hitting natural killers hard. plos-pone-0348709: Migratory birds fertilize wetlands with their droppings — along with phosphorus, antibiotic-resistance genes, and pathogens. This paper assessed the ecological risk of bird feces in a plateau wetland, speciating the phosphorus and screening for resistance genes and pathogens. The results weigh a natural nutrient source against its hidden hazards.
plos-pone-0357009: Knocking out the Lamp2 gene disrupts cellular recycling in mice — but does it reshape the gut microbiome? Shotgun metagenomic profiling of fecal samples found only limited genotype-associated differences under standard housing. The largely negative result narrows where Lamp2’s effects really act.
plos-pone-0357709: Liver failure rewrites the sugar tags on blood proteins. This paper mapped dysregulation of the serum and IgG N-glycome in decompensated cirrhosis and linked it to MELD-Na scores, the standard severity measure. The sugar signatures could sharpen prognosis for patients waiting on transplant lists.
plos-pone-0355409: Chronic kidney disease scars the kidneys through pericyte-driven fibrosis. plos-pone-0357909: Britain aspires to world-class behavioural research — but aspiration needs a plan. This paper identified strengths, challenges, and strategies for developing the UK’s capability through cross-sector workshops. The workshop synthesis charts a practical path forward for funders, universities, and industry alike.
plos-pone-0357309: Wrapping concrete columns in carbon fiber rings dramatically boosts their strength. This paper tested the compressive performance of CFRP ring-confined circular LSCFST columns under load. The experiments quantify exactly how much strength the carbon confinement adds — data engineers can build on.
plos-pone-0355209: When mothers are incarcerated, children pay a hidden price. This scoping review protocol will systematically map the impact of maternal incarceration on mothers and children. The planned review aims to inform policies that see the whole family — not just the sentence.
plos-pone-0357409: Quitting smoking may literally shrink an overgrown heart. This six-year retrospective observational study associated smoking cessation with regression of electrocardiographic left ventricular hypertrophy. The heart’s ability to heal after quitting is a powerful argument every smoker should hear.
plos-pone-0353309: Detecting objects in satellite imagery demands fusion that adapts to each scene. DAAF — dual-stream adaptive attention fusion with distribution alignment — tackles remote sensing object detection. The adaptive fusion sharpens detection across the bewildering variety of Earth observation imagery.
plos-pone-0344709: Differential expression analysis — finding which genes turn on or off — underpins modern biology, yet methods disagree constantly. This paper revisited the battlefield with an updated six-dimensional comparative study of the leading approaches. The six-axis comparison gives biologists the clearest map yet of which method to trust for which data.
plos-pone-0357109: Sepsis and postoperative delirium may share a hidden molecular bridge. This integrated transcriptomic profiling study implicated MAPK14/p38α as a candidate shared target at the sepsis–delirium interface, with computational validation. The shared target could one day let doctors treat — or prevent — both with one drug.
plos-pone-0355609: Ventilating ARDS patients — after trauma or surgery — is a high-stakes balancing act. This paper tested an electrical impedance tomography–guided individualized ventilation strategy in these patients. The imaging-guided personalization aims to ventilate injured lungs without inflicting further harm.
plos-pone-0355509: Racehorses deserve good lives after the track. This paper explored transforming retraining to support successful second careers for retired racehorses. The findings map what it takes — training, matching, aftercare — to turn athletes into companions. The work serves both equine welfare and the racing industry’s conscience.
plos-pone-0355109: Finding gastrointestinal stromal tumors in fused CT-PET scans demands AI that sees both modalities. This paper developed a Segformer-mix vision transformer for GIST segmentation in fused CT-PET images. The transformer-based segmentation promises more precise tumor mapping for surgical planning.
plos-pone-0356009: Poor bowel preparation ruins colonoscopies — and predicting it could prevent wasted procedures. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated risk prediction models for inadequate bowel prep. The synthesis identifies which models genuinely forecast prep failure — so high-risk patients get intensified regimens.
plos-pone-0354309: Tea estate workers in Bangladesh endure multidimensional energy poverty — lacking clean, reliable power in interlocking ways. This paper measured that poverty and its determinants at the household level. The findings expose energy injustice in the gardens that fill the world’s teacups.
plos-pone-0326409: Measuring disability for community rehabilitation — in Hong Kong — needs validated tools. This paper developed and validated the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule 2.0 for persons with disabilities using community rehab services. The validated instrument ensures services measure what matters to clients’ lives.
plos-pone-0352609: Bovine mastitis — udder infection — involves microRNAs worth measuring. This paper investigated miRNA expression in E. coli and coagulase-negative staphylococci mastitis cases. The findings reveal the molecular signatures distinguishing mastitis culprits — toward faster, targeted treatment.
plos-pone-0354709: Detecting joint inflammation — with cheap thermal cameras instead of expensive imaging. This paper developed texture-enhanced thermography for the task using consumer-grade cameras. The affordable approach could bring inflammation monitoring to clinics and homes that can’t afford MRI — democratizing rheumatology.
plos-pone-0354809: COVID-19 emergency patients — inflammatory blood indices predicting 30-day mortality, by age. This study tested their age-stratified prognostic performance in PCR-confirmed cases. The findings give emergency physicians simple blood markers that forecast who won’t survive — stratified by the age that matters most.
plos-pone-0354509: Oral cancer awareness in northwestern Italy — measured in community pharmacies. This cross-sectional survey assessed knowledge among adults. The findings reveal the awareness gaps that let a preventable, detectable cancer kill — and where education must go.
plos-pone-0352509: Hamstring strength assessment in sport — methods, post-activity decrements, asymmetry benchmarks. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized them. The findings standardized how the injury-prone muscle group gets measured. The research gives sports medicine the benchmarks distinguishing normal fatigue from injury risk.
plos-pone-0353909: LPG spherical tank vapor cloud explosions — behavior analyzed via multi-energy modeling and machine learning. This paper did so. The combined approach predicted blast consequences. The findings guided the safety engineering — containing the unthinkable where liquefied gas is stored.
plos-pone-0353609: Healthcare leadership, teamwork, and work outcomes — a model tested. This paper did so. The findings traced how leadership flows through teams to results. plos-pone-0352809: E-commerce time series — multitask learning for operational risk, demand forecasting, and anomaly detection. This paper built the framework. plos-pone-0349009: Aging behavior in reliability data — detected by an exact interpretable test. This paper built it. The findings distinguished true aging from noise. plos-pone-0351509: Pediatric bronchopneumonia — early differentiation by explainable machine learning on routine labs. This paper built it. The findings turned common blood tests into diagnostic clarity. The research served the children’s wards — the AI that shows its reasoning. plos-pone-0352209: Seven common weightlifting exercises — load-velocity profiles and exercise-specific velocity zones. This paper established them. The findings gave coaches the speed benchmarks. plos-pone-0353109: Thai patients with obesity — unrecognized myocardial infarction by cardiac MRI, prevalence and prognostic impact. This paper did so. The findings found the silent heart attacks. plos-pone-0348509: Semaglutide’s P29 intermediate — high-yield recombinant production via SNAC-tagged enterokinase-cleavable fusion peptides. This paper achieved it. plos-pone-0339109: Kidney transplant immunosuppression — regimens and long-term outcomes in a dual survival modeling framework. This paper studied them. The analysis modeled graft and patient survival jointly. Its transplant value is the regimen. The work balances rejection against the drugs’ toll.
plos-pone-0352309: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. plos-pone-0351409: Hearing loss and executive functions — results from a population-based cohort. This paper reported them. The analysis linked the ear to the executive. europmc-pmc2820409: Dengue can turn deadly when old antibodies help the virus instead of stopping it, a process called antibody enhancement. europmc-pmc2838909: Bed nets vowed to slash malaria, and this 2010 Kenya field check asks if mosquitoes truly thinned. europmc-pmc2846909: Gene-hunt math on filled-in DNA needs its own code. This 2010 paper brings ProbABEL, a pack for gene-wide hunts on filled data. The authors sketch its swift, sound sums. The tool met a daily need as fill-ins turned standard in gene work.
europmc-pmc2857309: Deaths from Clostridium difficile, a gut germ that strikes after antibiotics, were climbing. europmc-pmc2858209: The womb may screen embryos, rejecting weak ones before they settle. europmc-pmc2948509: A short DNA stretch can name almost any plant or animal. This 2010 paper champions the ITS2 region as the universal DNA barcode for plants and animals. europmc-pmc2988709: Sleeping sickness needs mapping, and this 2010 paper charts it. The authors build the Atlas of human African trypanosomiasis, mapping a neglected tropical disease. Their atlas guides control teams. The work aids elimination campaigns. Tsetse fly belts show up in sharp detail.
europmc-pmc3037909: Stroke research needs good models, and this 2011 review surveys them. The authors cover stroke biology, treatments, and lab models of human ischemic stroke. Their overview guides the field. The work shaped drug testing. Rat artery-block models lead the pack.

europmc-pmc3237409: Gut-survey studies got cleaner. This 2011 paper cuts PCR and sequencing artifacts in 16S rRNA studies. The authors' fixes sharpen the data. Their work spread through labs. Schloss's mothur carries the fixes. The paper is a methods staple. Thousands of studies use the pipeline.
europmc-pmc3278109: Tweets got tested as citation predictors. This 2011 paper asks whether tweets predict paper citations. The author reveals the link. Their work launched altmetrics. europmc-pmc3315009: Feeling in control got reviewed. This 2012 paper reviews how cues build our sense of agency. The authors map the cues. Their overview guides neuroscience. Illusions revealed the machinery. Moore's review is widely cited. It shaped schizophrenia research. The review is a classic.

europmc-pmc3378609: Private vs public care got compared. This 2012 review compares private and public health care in poor countries. The authors map the performance. Their overview guides policy. Basu's review is widely cited. It shaped health reform. The review is a classic.

europmc-pmc6588209: Psychedelics loosen the brain's grip on its own beliefs - and two big ideas explain how. europmc-pmc6624409: Tumors harbor rare cancer stem cells - self-renewing seeds that regrow the tumor after treatment. europmc-pmc6661709: Americans keep getting told to move more - but are they? Tracking national surveys against the 2018 Physical Activity Guidelines, researchers measured who hits the aerobic targets and who sits too much. The trends reveal stubborn gaps between guidelines and reality.
europmc-pmc6693809: Missing data plague every study - and the fashionable fix, multiple imputation, is not always best. europmc-pmc6720009: Schiff base chemistry - a click reaction that snaps together and pulls apart on demand - makes hydrogels that heal themselves. europmc-pmc6769509: Flavonoids - the pigments in berries, tea, and cocoa - may help tame blood sugar. europmc-pmc6787009: The brain's daydreaming circuit - the default-mode network - is its largest, yet maps of it disagreed. This study offers an improved anatomical model reconciling neuroimaging and lesion evidence. The reconciled map gives researchers a truer picture of the brain at rest.
europmc-pmc6827209: Tumors use a signal called AXL to grow, spread, and resist drugs. This review covers the AXL receptor tyrosine kinase: its functions, workings, and promise as an anti-cancer target. Blocking the signal could blunt many tumor tricks at once. One switch, many cancers - a tempting target.
europmc-pmc6876109: Tiny tags on DNA can tell your true age - but the clocks need rules. This paper probes DNA methyl tags aging clocks: their hurdles and fixes. The clocks of the DNA get their manual. True age gauges for doctors' tomorrow.
europmc-pmc6904909: E. coli learned to eat thin air - all its carbon from CO2. This study converted E. coli to generate all biomass carbon from CO2: the gut bug turned plant. The feat could green up industry. Synthetic autotrophy, achieved. A milestone for sustainable biomanufacturing.
europmc-pmc6979009: Tumor packs carry a looped RNA that drives liver cancer spread via boosting invading and vessel growth. The killer message in a bottle. The packs run cancer chatter. Pro-invasiveness tried in the lab. A roaming tell hopeful. Grab the message, halt the spread.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1209: Duty-free deals for poor nations — who used them, and did the watchers keep up? GAO's 2007 report grades America's trade-preference programs on both counts. The findings hand Congress the facts to decide which handouts to renew, which to retool, and whether the promised development payoff ever arrived.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-709: The Pentagon's grand strategy review needed sharper pencils, GAO's 2007 report says — and Congress needed to rewrite the assignment. The Quadrennial Defense Review's homework on future wars was thin in spots. The findings push both sides: better analysis from the brass, better questions from the Hill.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-909: The Vanuatu aid math did not add up in 2007 — GAO's report says the Millennium Challenge Corporation oversold the compact's projected impact. The findings deflate the development promises with harder numbers. The report is a field guide to spotting rosy forecasts in foreign aid deals.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-609: Most schools had a disaster plan on paper by 2007 — but GAO's report says districts would do better with stronger federal backup. The findings grade the state of school readiness. The report's message to Washington: help the schools drill like lives depend on it, because they do.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-309: The virtual border fence needed a real budget plan in 2007, and GAO's report says the SBInet spending plan had to better support oversight. The findings demand the numbers. The report warns that the electronic wall needed honest accounting. The fence of the future needed honest math.
gao-gaoreports-b-298609: Miramar Construction took its October 2006 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Builders get the same full hearing as everyone.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-709: Rust was eating the military's stockpiled gear in 2006, and GAO's report says more measures against corrosion could save money. The findings do the math. The report warns that the prepositioned assets should not rot in their sheds. The corrosion had to be fought.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-309: Disabled vets' jobless pay needed better handling in 2006, and GAO's report says the VA should run the program tighter. The findings demand the discipline. The report warns that the hurt veterans deserved careful care. The stewardship had to be careful.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-209: Army repair shipments needed better controls in 2006, and GAO's report says internal controls for items sent to contractors had to be strengthened. The findings target the gaps. The report warns that the parts pipeline should not leak. The controls had to be strengthened.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-109: The FDA's morning-after pill call got a GAO review in 2005, and the report examines the decision process to deny over-the-counter marketing. The findings trace the denial. The report warns that the emergency contraceptive deserved a fair process. The process had to be examined.
openalex-w7204863209: Taking medicine without a prescription is common in Brazil, and this article examines what that habit costs. Reviewing the literature on self-medication, the authors analyze the associated factors, the risks, and the consequences for public health. The study treats self-medication as a collective problem rather than an individual failing. A clear-eyed look at why people skip the doctor and what happens when they do.
openalex-w7205002709: What causes autism is still one of medicine's hardest questions, and the immune system is emerging as a suspect. This systematic review examines the evidence linking maternal immune activation during pregnancy to autism risk in children. The authors synthesize studies on how immune disruption might alter fetal brain development. Careful and current, it evaluates a leading hypothesis without overstating what the science can yet prove.
openalex-w7152572309: Sepsis can cloud the brain, and early signs matter. This study profiled neurological dysfunction in adults arriving at the ER with sepsis, hunting early clinical, lab, and imaging clues. The authors mapped the warning patterns. An emergency-medicine study of the brain under septic siege.
openalex-w7171565009: Straightening a bent spine risks the spinal cord. This study tested whether two nerve-monitoring signals together predict injury better than one during scoliosis surgery. The authors measured motor evoked potentials against muscle responses. A surgical-safety study of double-checking the cord.
openalex-w7210294609: Sepsis throws clotting into chaos, and new thinking is emerging. This paper opens the door to modern management of sepsis-induced coagulopathy, a dynamic clotting disorder. The authors surveyed the evolving science. A hematology review of taming blood gone rogue.
openalex-w4416290809: Heat illness is rising with the planet's fever. This paper covers spotting and treating it, from mild cramps to deadly heatstroke, mixing bedside know-how with molecule-level science. The authors blended both views. A medical review of taming heat's harms today.
arxiv-2606-16009: Human interpreters at conferences handle things machines still miss: timing, tone, and knowing what to skip. This paper studies the craft of professional interpreting and draws lessons for designing AI interpreting systems. The author argues that machine interpreting must learn from human practice, not just from transcripts, to become truly usable.
arxiv-2606-16109: A combinatorics paper about flag spheres — layered geometric structures built from nested sets — and the largest sets of points within them with no two connected (independent sets). The author proves results about how large such sets can be. It is a pure mathematics result aimed at specialists in combinatorics and discrete geometry.
arxiv-2606-16409: Retrieval-augmented AI agents search knowledge graphs for facts, but the retriever's idea of "good results" may not match what the agent needs. PathRouter aligns the training rewards with actual retrieval quality in agentic graph RAG systems. The paper targets AI researchers building agents that reason over structured knowledge.
arxiv-2606-16609: Random matrices have a famous "circular law" for their eigenvalues, but a few eigenvalues escape the circle — outliers. This probability paper studies the stability of those outliers: how much they wobble under perturbations. It targets random-matrix theorists in mathematics and mathematical physics.
arxiv-2606-16709: Scientific computing still runs largely on Fortran, but modern Fortran lacked low-precision floating point — the fast, compact arithmetic AI made popular. This paper enables low-precision arithmetic in modern Fortran, bringing the language's number-crunching up to date. It targets HPC programmers who want speed without leaving Fortran.
arxiv-2606-16809: Training AI on private data risks leaking it — and AI accelerators (systolic arrays) weren't built for privacy. DataGuard guarantees private training on such accelerators: the hardware itself enforces the privacy. It is for hardware and privacy researchers. Privacy in silicon, not just software.
